body:
> First, I have to say that I am really impressed by what you guys are doing here. Also, your docs are outstanding and easy to follow. I spotted your project on my recommendations page and immediately fell in love, losing most of my Friday night tinkering around.

Awesome! It's great to hear that. Thanks for writing it :smile: 

> When I got to your file upload section in the docs, I hit a snag when trying to upload an mp4 file.

Thanks for the very detailed bug report.

The bug was because of a default constraint in Pydantic. I just created a custom internal class for this that fixes the problem. I also added a test for this specific use case.

Please try with the latest version `0.1.17`.

---

I also plan on supporting Starlette's (undocumented) file uploads, to get a file-like object. But this will come afterwards.

Great, thanks! `0.1.17` works without a hitch :tada:. I'll close this issue and keep an eye out for changes in the future. 

> I also plan on supporting Starlette's (undocumented) file uploads, to get a file-like object. But this will come afterwards.

That looks like a good idea. Do you have any plans to reuse [pathlib's file interface](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path.write_bytes)?

Awesome! Thanks for reporting back.

I'll use [Starlette's undocumented `UploadFile`](https://github.com/encode/starlette/blob/master/starlette/formparsers.py#L38) which exposes a nice file-like API. So it will be quite similar to standard Python files.

issue.title: reusable requestBody support

repository.name: fastapi
repository.description: FastAPI framework, high performance, easy to learn, fast to code, ready for production

issue.body:
Hi,
**Expected result:**
my goal is to organize request bodies under components/requestBodies, [allowed by openapi 3x ](https://swagger.io/docs/specification/components/)
So for the end-result my openapi schema would have these:
1. a ref to #/components/requestBodies/<MYREQUESTBODY> in the requestBody field of the corresponding path operation decorator
2. the request body itself (which would contain the same info as in requestBody field, but  would be named). the location of the body, of course, would be #/components/requestBodies

**Findings:**
it seems that [this line](https://github.com/tiangolo/fastapi/blob/06e42a4e5de9facf6061cb47d5c34c36a58fa898/fastapi/openapi/utils.py#L120) of get_openapi_operation_request_body() method states, that ref_prefix is hardcoded to a constant REF_PREFIX, which is #/components/schemas.
Hence my goal #1 above becomes impossible (of course if I'm not missing something).

for #2 I didn't find any pythonic way to move requestBody objects under #/components/requestBodies. 
Of course I understand that I can always do that manually by updating the get_openapi() output. but that doesn't seem right either.

Please help to understand how these issues can be resolved.
I assume this would be an enhancement request, unless I'm missing something

--thanks

issue.title: fastapi doesn't use host passed to uvicorn

repository.name: fastapi
repository.description: FastAPI framework, high performance, easy to learn, fast to code, ready for production

issue.body:
FastApi output log shows a host different from the one supplied to uvicorn. 

Two computers, both running fastapi. I log into computer #1 through an SSH tunnel and run fastapi using host-x. I log into computer #1 again and then ssh into computer #2 and run fastapi there using a different host-y. I then send requests to the different hosts, each of which returns 200 OK.

The problem is that fastapi running on computer #2 uses the host corresponding to the computer #1 host even though uvicorn is supplied a different host. If I add a third computer logged into from computer #1, the same thing happens.

One difference is that the host on computer#1 is shown in the eth0 section of ifconfig whereas the host on computer #2 is shown in the wlan0 section of ifconfig. So maybe fastapi is somehow resolving the wlan0 host of computer #2 to the eth0 host of computer #1 on the other side of the ssh connection.

Ultimately, how can I force fastapi to use the same host as uvicorn? Where is fastapi picking up computer #1's host? Is this purely a networking problem, or can fastapi take a parameter (that I haven't found) that makes sure that uvicorn and fastapi agree on the host? The code currently initializes the FastAPI object with no arguments.

### running on computer #1 (logged into through ssh tunnel)
(venv) gary@batterypi:~/thenthis $ python run.py --host **192.168.1.94**
INFO:     Started server process [23966]
